qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2351 established safeguard measures concerning ferroalloys, including ferro-silicon (FeSi). Article 7 provides for a review no later than one year after the entry into force of those measures. According to EUROALLIAGES, EU producers of metallic silicon are scaling back or halting production, which risks the permanent loss of industrial capacity and increased dependence on supplies from China. The growing substitution of FeSi with imported silicon also undermines the effectiveness of safeguard measures concerning ferro-silicon. The situation is exacerbated by high energy costs and the EU ETS. The industry highlights the need to expedite the R869 anti-dumping review concerning silicon from China, as well as the risk of stockpiling ahead of the introduction of stricter measures. It also stresses the importance of stable European supplies for industrial customers. In view of the above: 1.
As part of the review provided for under Article 7, is the Commission considering a 50 % reduction in quotas for ferro-alloys and the adjustment of the pricing mechanism?

What steps will the Commission take to counter the increasing substitution of FeSi with imported metallic silicon and prevent the permanent shutdown of EU production capacity for this strategic raw material and increased dependence on Chinese supplies?

Will the Commission expedite the R869 investigation, examine imports from Angola and, in accordance with the relevant procedures, consider provisional measures and the registration of imports in view of the risk of stockpiling?
